messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: elevated DNS SERVFAILs and timeouts observed for geo-routed records in eu-central-1. Error rate threshold crossed (7.2%). Paging @sam_oncall.

sam_oncall: Acknowledged. Checking metrics and customer reports. Which provider is acting up? CF or Route53?

maria_net: Early signs point to mixed failures. Our probes show Cloudflare returning REFUSED from certain PoPs and Route53 showing delayed propagation for failover records. Correlation: failures spike for queries routed through eu-central-1 AZc egress.

jess_ops: I see a surge in upstream retries on the resolver fleet in eu-central-1. Application telemetry shows increased DNS lookup latency and websocket disconnects around the same window.

alex_prodeng: Could be an AZ egress networking congestion combined with an external resolver cluster problem. Suggest immediate short-term mitigation: demote AZc from geodns so clients don't resolve to that egress. Who can change geodns?

sam_oncall: I can. Plan: 1) set AZc weight to 0 2) post status update 3) open vendor tickets 4) start packet capture on NAT hosts. Execute now.

jess_ops: Applying change to geodns pool. Command: ```POST /api/geodns/modify {region: "eu-central-1", az: "c", weight: 0}```. Config pushed. TTL for these entries is 20s so change should take effect quickly.

maria_net: after change: queries to AZc dropped ~85% within 35s. Total SERVFAIL down from 7.2% -> 1.5%. App-timeout reports reduced but a handful of long-tail failures remain.

route53-bot: Created AWS case SR-778122 for suspected Route53 propagation delays in eu-central-1. Attach logs: /internal/sr/778122/logs.tar.gz.

priya_support: Customer update ready: "We experienced DNS resolution instability in EU causing intermittent API timeouts. Traffic has been routed away from the affected egress and we are monitoring. We will provide updates as we have them." Post to status page? :warning:

sam_oncall: Post it, include that we're tracking vendor tickets with expected update within 60m.

alex_prodeng: Also opened Cloudflare ticket CF-9981 for REFUSED responses from specific PoPs. Shared tcpdump we captured. Their team asked for exact PoP IPs and times; I uploaded pcap to the ticket.

jess_ops: Started tcpdump on the eu NATs: ```sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 53 and host 203.0.113.45 -w /tmp/euc_nat_dns.pcap``` Capturing 120s per request.

maria_net: note: I noticed some of our internal resolver instances hit file descriptor limits and were restarting slowly; reconfiguring ulimit and rolling fixed nodes now. This may have amplified the symptoms. Rolling patch applied to 2 instances.

sam_oncall: thanks. That's important — add that to the post-incident review. For now keep AZc out. If vendor says resolved, we'll slowly reintroduce with small weight and monitor 15m.

route53-bot: Route53 support responded: "We've observed elevated propagation latencies for certain failover records in eu-central-1. Investigating routing plane. ETA update 45m."

priya_support: Posted status update + customer DM batch. Several large customers acknowledged and asked for RCA; flagged to Alex for follow-up.

alex_prodeng: I'll own postmortem and customer RCA. Quick note: recommend we automate fallback to cross-region resolver pool in case external provider instability is detected. Low-scope item for Optimize team.

jess_ops: Observability: error rate now stable at ~1.2% post-mitigation. Websocket disconnects mostly resolved. Keeping watch.

maria_net: continuing probe loop from multiple vantage points: a few CF PoPs still show intermittent REFUSED but less frequent. Also uploaded tcpdump to CF ticket.

sam_oncall: good. We'll keep this incident open until vendors confirm. Handoff plan: I'll stay for 30m, then hand to @maria_net for monitoring if stable. Alex, please prepare RCA skeleton. Priya, keep customers updated.

incident-bot: Incident update recorded: geodns AZc weight set to 0 at 6295000020, Cloudflare CF-9981, AWS SR-778122. Assigned postmortem owner: alex_prodeng.

priya_support: updating ticket queue and closing temporary customer notes.

alex_prodeng: drafting RCA outline: timeline, root cause hypotheses (external resolver + internal FD exhaustion), mitigations taken, follow-ups (automation, ulimit hardening), and customer impact summary.

jess_ops: standing by for revert testing when vendors confirm. Will run synthetic checks and a small canary traffic test.

maria_net: pcap and logs uploaded to both vendors. Continuing 1m probes. If we see >2% error rate again we'll escalate to full failover to non-EU replicas.

sam_oncall: thanks team — moving to watch mode. Handoff to @maria_net at +30m if no regressions.
